practiceNotes: Spaced recall maintains definitions, representations, assumptions and method selection; independently assess proofs, programs, experiments and extended analyses.

Use cumulative unseen tasks, uncertainty reports, failed-model analysis and reproducible notebooks or laboratory records. Distinguish operating a package from implementing an algorithm or proving a guarantee.
Laboratories require suitable facilities, trained supervision, risk assessment and locally approved procedures. Simulated data support preparation but do not certify hands-on laboratory competence.
Biological work uses approved low-risk organisms and materials. Human, animal, genomic and field studies require applicable consent, welfare, collection, data-governance and ethics approvals.
Security exercises require owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. No assessment authorizes testing third-party infrastructure.
Radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure systems and hazardous chemicals require facility-specific training and authorization.
Team projects should retain individually assessed contributions, accessible alternatives and auditable data and code provenance.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect molecular chemistry to biological function.
decks.title: Biochemistry and Metabolism

outcomes.description: Read sequence and three-dimensional representations of proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids; relate folding, domains and noncovalent binding to function.
Apply explicitly taught binding and Michaelis-Menten models; estimate affinities and kinetic parameters by grid-based residual minimization and distinguish inhibition models and limitations.
Trace atoms, electrons and energy through respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthetic pathways; calculate coupling and interpret isotope or metabolite perturbation evidence.

practice: Analyze enzyme and isotope-tracing datasets, map carbon and energy balances and distinguish kinetic limitation from thermodynamic feasibility.

includes: Population growth, species interactions, behavioral strategies, ecosystem flows and ecological sampling.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain ecological dynamics and infer processes in the field.
decks.title: Ecology

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete exponential and density-dependent population changes, life-table survival and simple competition or predator-prey updates with stated assumptions.
Analyze food webs, nutrient and energy budgets, succession and spatial disturbance; compare behavioral strategies through explicit fitness and resource tradeoffs.
Design quadrat, transect and repeated-observation studies; distinguish detection, environmental covariation and causal effects using appropriate sampling and uncertainty analysis.

practice: Conduct or analyze a replicated ecological survey and test competing resource, interaction and sampling explanations for an observed pattern.

includes: Floating-point error, linear and nonlinear solvers, interpolation, quadrature and ODE integration.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Implement reliable numerical approximations.
decks.title: Numerical Analysis

outcomes.description: Implement pivoted elimination, iterative linear solvers and bracketed or Newton root finding; assess conditioning, residuals and convergence criteria.
Implement polynomial or spline interpolation and numerical quadrature; derive elementary error estimates and diagnose instability or insufficient resolution.
Implement Euler, Runge-Kutta and implicit ODE steps; analyze consistency, stability regions and convergence with refinement and known solutions.

practice: Develop a tested numerical library and an error study that separates model error, conditioning, discretization and roundoff.

includes: Convexity, constrained optimization, linear programming, duality and gradient-based algorithms.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Formulate and solve continuous optimization problems.
decks.title: Optimization

outcomes.description: Establish convexity and derive first- or second-order optimality, Lagrange multiplier and KKT conditions; formulate linear programs and interpret dual certificates.
Implement gradient, Newton and projected methods with line search; prove elementary convex convergence bounds and diagnose scaling, nonconvexity and constraint failures.

practice: Solve constrained estimation and resource-allocation problems, comparing algorithm traces with optimality certificates and sensitivity analysis.

includes: Likelihood and Bayesian inference, multivariate distributions, linear and generalized linear models, diagnostics and statistical decisions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Derive and validate statistical estimators and models.
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics

outcomes.description: Derive likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimators, sufficiency, bias, consistency and elementary information bounds; calculate multivariate Gaussian conditioning and posterior uncertainty.
Implement linear and logistic regression using matrix and Newton formulations; diagnose residuals, collinearity, model misspecification and predictive uncertainty.
Compare tests, intervals and losses; control multiple testing and distinguish predictive, causal and decision claims under observational or randomized designs.

practice: Derive and implement an estimator, audit its simulation coverage and analyze a multivariable dataset with sensitivity and decision analysis.

includes: Three-dimensional particle and rigid-body mechanics, constrained variation, Hamiltonian dynamics and nonlinear stability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive advanced classical motion from geometric and variational models.
decks.title: Analytical Classical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Solve central-force, rotating-frame and rigid-body problems using generalized coordinates, inertia tensors and angular momentum.
Derive Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton equations, constraints, conserved quantities and Poisson-bracket relations; connect symmetries to conservation through Noether's theorem.
Analyze coupled normal modes, nonlinear phase portraits, resonance and elementary chaotic sensitivity; distinguish local stability from global behavior.

practice: Derive and analyze a constrained three-dimensional mechanism and compare Newtonian, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian descriptions.

includes: Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields, boundary-value methods, Maxwell equations, waves and radiation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict electromagnetic fields in space and matter.
decks.title: Electromagnetic Field Theory

outcomes.description: Solve electrostatic and magnetostatic problems using potentials, images, multipole expansions and explicitly developed separation of variables in Cartesian or spherical geometry.
Derive integral and differential Maxwell equations, material boundary conditions, energy flow and plane-wave propagation in vacuum and simple media.
Calculate elementary waveguide modes, dipole radiation and polarization; relate source distributions and measured angular or spectral patterns.

practice: Solve a boundary-value field problem by two methods and infer a simple source geometry from supplied field measurements.

includes: Thermal state variables, laws, entropy, potentials, engines and elementary microscopic ensembles.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect heat, work and entropy to microscopic states.
decks.title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Foundations

outcomes.description: Apply thermodynamic laws to gases, cycles and phase changes; derive entropy and free-energy relations and evaluate reversible bounds and stability.
Construct microcanonical and canonical probabilities and partition functions for ideal gases, spins and oscillators; calculate energy, pressure, entropy and fluctuations.

practice: Analyze an engine and a microscopic heat-capacity model, reconciling macroscopic measurements with state-counting assumptions.

includes: Quantum state and measurement postulates, spatial Schrödinger equations, spin, angular momentum and approximation methods.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate elementary quantum behavior and its measurable consequences.
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Use complex state vectors, Hermitian operators, basis changes and unitary evolution to calculate measurement probabilities and uncertainty.
Solve and normalize one-dimensional well, barrier and harmonic-oscillator states; calculate tunneling, currents and wave-packet evolution.
Separate the three-dimensional central-potential equation in spherical coordinates; calculate hydrogenic and spin states and elementary angular-momentum coupling.
Apply nondegenerate perturbation and variational methods; explain identical-particle symmetry and derive elementary dipole transition rules.

practice: Solve a spatial bound-state problem and estimate a perturbed energy or transition strength, checking normalization, dimensions and approximation validity.

includes: Calibration, spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis and chemical identification.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Choose and validate methods for chemical composition measurements.
decks.title: Analytical and Instrumental Chemistry

outcomes.description: Construct external, internal-standard and standard-addition calibrations; estimate recovery, uncertainty, detection limits and matrix effects.
Explain and operate bounded UV-visible, IR, NMR, mass-spectrometric, chromatographic and potentiometric methods using taught response, separation and detection models.
Infer identities and mixture composition from complementary measurements; select confirmatory evidence and distinguish resolution, selectivity and sensitivity.

practice: Design and validate an unknown-mixture analysis using two complementary methods, calibration controls and a defended uncertainty budget.

includes: Periodic chemistry, coordination bonding, main-group reactions, crystal structures and inorganic synthesis reasoning.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain inorganic structure and reactivity using working models.
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Compare main-group and transition-element chemistry using periodicity, acid-base models, redox diagrams and bonding representations.
Assign coordination geometries, oxidation states, isomers and d-electron configurations; use explicitly taught crystal-field splitting to predict magnetism and qualitative spectra.
Describe unit cells, coordination numbers, lattice energetics and common defects; predict simple inorganic preparation and stability from equilibrium and redox evidence.

practice: Identify an inorganic compound from structural, magnetic and reaction evidence and propose a balanced, thermodynamically justified preparation.

includes: Chemical potentials, nonideal mixtures, phase equilibria, electrochemistry, rate mechanisms and simple transport.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Derive thermodynamic and kinetic models of chemical systems.
decks.title: Physical Chemical Thermodynamics and Kinetics

outcomes.description: Derive equilibrium relations from chemical potentials; calculate activities, phase diagrams, colligative effects and electrochemical potentials with explicit standard-state conventions.
Derive well-mixed mechanism rate equations, steady-state and pre-equilibrium approximations, Arrhenius fits and one-dimensional steady diffusion; diagnose parameter identifiability.

practice: Fit competing reaction mechanisms and construct a nonideal phase or electrochemical model, reporting uncertainty and approximation failures.

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular orbitals, electronic approximations, rotational-vibrational spectra and point-group symmetry.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect molecular quantum models to structure and spectroscopy.
decks.title: Molecular Quantum Chemistry and Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Derive small-basis variational molecular-orbital equations and calculate elementary bonding energies; distinguish Born-Oppenheimer, Hartree-Fock and density-functional approximations.
Calculate rigid-rotor, harmonic and elementary anharmonic spectra and electronic transition intensities; infer bond lengths, force constants and electronic structure.
Assign molecular point groups and use explicitly constructed symmetry operations and character tables to obtain orbital combinations and vibrational selection rules.

practice: Derive and solve a small molecular-orbital model and jointly interpret rotational, vibrational and electronic spectral evidence.

includes: Microbial growth, cultivation, metabolism, genetic exchange, viruses and host interactions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Study microbial mechanisms and their ecological or health consequences.
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology

outcomes.description: Plan approved low-risk culture, staining, enumeration and identification workflows; calculate growth and dilution and interpret contamination and cultivation bias.
Explain bacterial and archaeal metabolic diversity, horizontal gene transfer, microbial communities and viral replication from molecular evidence.
Compare colonization, infection, resistance and transmission mechanisms; evaluate antimicrobial susceptibility and prevention claims without making clinical treatment recommendations.

practice: Analyze a contained microbial identification and growth study, including controls and a mechanistic interpretation of susceptibility data.

includes: Membranes, organelles, cytoskeleton, trafficking, signaling, cell cycle, apoptosis and cellular disease mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer cellular organization and regulation from mechanistic evidence.
decks.title: Cell Biology

outcomes.description: Explain compartmentation, cytoskeletal mechanics and membrane transport or trafficking; interpret localization, fractionation and live-cell imaging experiments.
Construct receptor-to-response signaling diagrams with feedback and cross-talk; distinguish pathway order and causal dependence using perturbation and rescue experiments.
Explain cell-cycle control, differentiation, apoptosis and oncogenic disruption; compare competing cellular mechanisms against time-course and intervention evidence.

practice: Analyze imaging and perturbation datasets to infer a trafficking or signaling mechanism and design a decisive rescue experiment.

includes: Population genetics, selection, drift, phylogenetic inference, adaptation, speciation and macroevolution.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain and infer evolutionary change.
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology

outcomes.description: Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations and finite-generation selection, mutation and migration recurrences; compare drift through explicitly taught finite-population sampling models.
Construct small parsimony and distance trees and calculate likelihoods under a taught independent-site substitution model; assess uncertainty, homoplasy and model limits.
Evaluate adaptation, sexual selection, speciation and historical explanations using comparative, fossil, genomic and experimental evidence rather than just-so narratives.

practice: Compare demographic and selective explanations for allele data and defend a phylogenetic interpretation with explicit competing models.

includes: Plant transport, photosynthesis, nutrition, hormones, reproduction and environmental physiology.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain and measure plant function and growth.
decks.title: Plant Physiology and Development

outcomes.description: Calculate water-potential and mass-balance consequences for xylem, phloem, stomata and mineral uptake; interpret photosynthetic gas-exchange and light-response measurements.
Explain meristems, hormone signaling, flowering, reproduction and stress responses; connect tissue organization and life cycles to plant growth strategies.
Design controlled plant growth or transport experiments, accounting for acclimation, developmental stage, environmental gradients and destructive-sampling effects.

practice: Measure a plant environmental response and reconcile gas exchange, water balance and growth evidence under competing physiological explanations.

includes: Comparative organ systems, transport, electrophysiology, endocrine feedback, reproduction and physiological integration.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Predict integrated animal function with bounded quantitative models.
decks.title: Comparative Animal Physiology

outcomes.description: Apply locally developed pressure-flow, diffusion, filtration and mass-balance equations to circulation, respiration, digestion, renal function and osmoregulation; state their limits.
Calculate membrane equilibrium potentials and conductance-based currents using taught ionic models; explain action potentials, synapses and muscle contraction.
Analyze endocrine, reproductive and thermal feedback and compare animal adaptations; predict integrated responses to exercise, dehydration or environmental stress.

practice: Analyze a multichannel physiological time series and defend a causal account using transport balances, membrane models and feedback predictions.

includes: Fate specification, pattern formation, lineage, morphogenesis, regeneration and comparative development.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain construction and variation of multicellular form.
decks.title: Developmental Biology

outcomes.description: Infer lineage, competence, induction and positional information from transplantation, lineage tracing and gene perturbations; interpret explicitly taught gradient-threshold models.
Explain cell movement, adhesion, tissue folding, organogenesis and regeneration; compare developmental mechanisms across model organisms and distinguish conserved from convergent outcomes.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage images and perturbations, then design a spatially and temporally controlled discrimination experiment.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, antigen recognition, immune regulation, immunopathology and assay interpretation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain immune responses and evaluate intervention evidence.
decks.title: Immunology

outcomes.description: Trace antigen recognition, presentation, lymphocyte activation and effector responses; explain receptor diversity, tissue organization and host-pathogen interactions.
Explain memory, tolerance, inflammation, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and tumor immunity through cellular and molecular regulatory mechanisms.
Interpret antibody, flow-cytometry and cellular-response assays with controls; evaluate vaccine or immunotherapy evidence and justify benefit-risk conclusions.

practice: Analyze a blinded immune-assay panel and compare mechanistic explanations and intervention evidence, including false-positive and population-risk considerations.

includes: Automata and grammars, computability, reductions, decidability and elementary complexity classes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Establish computational possibilities and limits.
decks.title: Theory of Computation

outcomes.description: Construct finite and pushdown automata and regular or context-free grammars; prove language-class membership and nonmembership with closure or pumping arguments.
Represent computation with Turing machines; prove undecidability and recognizability claims through diagonalization and many-one reductions.
Define time and space complexity, P, NP and completeness; construct polynomial reductions and distinguish evidence from unproved complexity conjectures.

practice: Write complete language and reduction proofs and construct executable small-machine examples that clarify the limits of testing.

includes: Language semantics, lexical and grammar models, parsing, typing, intermediate representations and runtime support.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Implement a small programming language and its execution model.
decks.title: Programming Languages and Compilers

outcomes.description: Specify evaluation order, scope, closures, mutation and type rules; compare procedural, functional and object-oriented language behavior through interpreters.
Construct finite-state lexers and grammar-based parsers, type-check syntax trees and lower them into an intermediate representation and machine-level code.
Implement stack frames and closures and explain tracing garbage collection and basic data-flow optimization with preservation tests.

practice: Implement a typed interpreter and small compiler, testing lexical scope, error reporting, optimization preservation and runtime memory behavior.

includes: Layered networks, routing, reliable transport, congestion, sockets, RPC and basic distributed failure models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Build communicating programs and reason about network behavior.
decks.title: Networks and Distributed Computing Foundations

outcomes.description: Calculate addressing, forwarding and routing behavior; explain framing, link errors, IP, naming and application protocols using packet traces.
Implement socket applications and a simulated reliable transport protocol; analyze loss, delay, retransmission, flow control and congestion.
Use RPC, logical clocks and elementary replication; distinguish partial failure, duplicate execution and ordering from single-machine concurrency.

practice: Build a networked service and protocol simulator with loss and delay injection, documenting observable behavior and failure assumptions.

includes: Threat models, practical cryptographic interfaces, system and application defenses, privacy and authorized testing.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Assess and reduce security risks in functioning systems.
decks.title: Security and Privacy Engineering

outcomes.description: Construct assets, adversary and trust-boundary models; correctly use encryption, authenticated transport, hashes, signatures and password-storage interfaces with nonce and key requirements.
Demonstrate and remediate memory, injection, authentication, authorization and network flaws in isolated systems; validate defenses through negative tests and logging.
Compare disclosure, monitoring, privacy and availability obligations; justify proportionate controls and residual-risk acceptance with evidence.

practice: Audit an intentionally vulnerable local application, implement fixes and produce a reproducible authorized test report and risk decision.

includes: State-space search, heuristic guarantees, constraints, symbolic knowledge, planning and adversarial games.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct symbolic agents from explicit problem representations.
decks.title: Search, Reasoning and Planning

outcomes.description: Represent states, actions and costs; implement uniform-cost, A-star and constraint search and prove conditions for completeness or optimality.
Represent knowledge in propositional and restricted first-order forms; implement unification, resolution or rule inference and explain soundness and search limitations.
Implement classical planning and minimax with pruning; compare representations, heuristics and agent objectives on adversarial or resource-limited tasks.

practice: Build a planning or game agent, prove a bounded guarantee and investigate failures caused by representation and heuristic choices.

includes: Supervised learning, latent-variable inference, neural networks, reinforcement learning and responsible model evaluation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Build predictive and decision models with defensible evaluation.
decks.title: Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Implement regularized regression, trees and kernel methods; select models with leakage-free validation and evaluate calibration, subgroup errors and deployment consequences.
Implement clustering, principal-component reduction and finite-mixture EM; calculate inference in small Bayesian networks and diagnose latent-model identifiability.
Derive and implement backpropagation for feedforward networks; train with a documented framework and diagnose optimization, overfitting and representation failures.
Formulate finite Markov decision processes; implement value iteration and tabular Q-learning and assess exploration, reward misspecification and off-policy evaluation limits.

practice: Implement baselines and a learned system on held-out data or a finite simulator, reporting ablations, uncertainty and an evidence-based deployment decision.

includes: User research, interaction design, accessibility, prototyping, empirical evaluation and sociotechnical judgment.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Design and assess useful, accessible human-facing systems.
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction

outcomes.description: Conduct consent-based interviews and observation; code qualitative evidence and translate conflicting needs into testable interaction requirements.
Construct interactive prototypes using task models, feedback, error recovery and accessibility principles; justify choices for diverse users and contexts.
Design usability studies and controlled comparisons, analyze qualitative and quantitative evidence and justify changes considering privacy, exclusion and persuasive-design harms.

practice: Research, prototype and evaluate an accessible interface with consenting participants or approved proxy evidence and an individually defended redesign.

includes: Three-dimensional geometry, camera projection, rasterization, ray tracing, sampling, image operations and visualization.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct images and visual explanations from geometric data.
decks.title: Computer Graphics and Visualization

outcomes.description: Implement homogeneous-coordinate transformations, camera projection, clipping, rasterization and visibility for three-dimensional polygonal scenes.
Implement ray intersections and deterministic illumination integration using explicitly taught radiance and reflection models; diagnose aliasing, sampling and numerical artifacts.
Apply discrete image filtering and color representations; design quantitative visualizations and justify encodings against distortion, accessibility and uncertainty requirements.

practice: Build a small renderer and scientific visualization, validating geometry numerically and explaining perceptual and approximation limitations.

includes: Holomorphic functions, complex integration, residues, analytic continuation and conformal maps.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Use analytic structure to prove and calculate complex-variable results.
decks.title: Complex Analysis

outcomes.description: Verify complex differentiability and Cauchy-Riemann conditions; prove elementary consequences of analyticity and power-series representations.
Prove and apply Cauchy integral results, Laurent expansions and residue calculations with contour and singularity conditions.
Evaluate real integrals and inverse-transform examples by contours; construct simple conformal maps and analyze branches and analytic continuation.

practice: Write contour proofs and solve a planar mapping or transform problem, identifying branch choices and invalid contour deformations.

includes: Topological spaces, continuity, compactness, connectedness, quotient spaces, fundamental groups and coverings.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Reason about continuity and global shape.
decks.title: Topology

outcomes.description: Construct and compare metric, product and quotient topologies; prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties with counterexamples.
Calculate fundamental groups of elementary spaces using homotopy and van Kampen arguments; relate covering spaces to lifting and noncontractible loops.

practice: Analyze a family of quotient spaces and prove that selected spaces cannot be homeomorphic using explicit invariants.

includes: Curves, surfaces, local charts, tangent spaces, metrics, tensors and elementary differential forms.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Calculate geometric quantities independently of coordinates.
decks.title: Differential Geometry

outcomes.description: Calculate arc length, curvature, torsion, surface fundamental forms and Gaussian curvature; distinguish intrinsic from embedding-dependent quantities.
Use smooth charts, tangent and cotangent bases, tensor transformations and differential forms; calculate metric lengths, pullbacks and coordinate-invariant integrals.

practice: Compute the same curved-surface quantities in two coordinate charts and prove their appropriate transformation or invariance.

includes: Divisibility, prime factorization, congruences, quadratic residues and elementary Diophantine equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Prove and calculate arithmetic structure.
decks.title: Number Theory

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Euclidean algorithms, unique factorization, modular inverses, Chinese remaindering and Euler or Fermat congruences.
Solve selected integer equations and quadratic congruences; use orders, quadratic reciprocity and elementary prime-distribution estimates with stated limitations.

practice: Produce proof-based solutions to congruence and Diophantine problems, including counterexamples to unjustified generalizations.

includes: Generating functions, combinatorial structures, extremal graph theory and probabilistic existence methods.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Analyze large families of finite structures.
decks.title: Advanced Combinatorics and Graph Theory

outcomes.description: Construct ordinary and exponential generating functions and extract coefficients for recurrences, partitions and labeled structures.
Prove matching, extremal and coloring results; use expectation, alteration and random-graph models to establish existence and threshold estimates.

practice: Solve an enumeration problem by two representations and write a probabilistic existence proof with a constructive comparison.

includes: Linear elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic PDEs; transforms, characteristics, boundary conditions and finite discretizations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Solve spatial evolution and boundary-value problems.
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations

outcomes.description: Derive and solve transport, wave, heat and Laplace equations using characteristics, separation, Fourier transforms and Green functions in one to three dimensions.
Implement finite-difference and finite-volume schemes with explicit boundary conditions; analyze consistency, von Neumann stability and convergence through manufactured solutions.

practice: Solve a two-dimensional boundary or transport problem analytically where possible and numerically, reporting boundary, stability and refinement checks.

includes: Measures, Lebesgue integration, Lp spaces, Banach and Hilbert spaces, operator theory and abstract variational problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Develop rigorous infinite-dimensional analytic foundations.
decks.title: Measure Theory and Functional Analysis

outcomes.description: Construct measures and Lebesgue integrals; prove and apply convergence, product-measure and Radon-Nikodym results with precise hypotheses.
Analyze Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality and bounded or compact operators; prove core uniform-boundedness, open-mapping and Hilbert-space spectral results.
Formulate coercive bilinear variational problems; prove existence and uniqueness through Hilbert-space representation and derive Galerkin error bounds.

practice: Write a measure-convergence proof and a Hilbert-space existence argument, then demonstrate exactly where each fails without a key hypothesis.

includes: Galois theory, modules, representations, commutative algebra and affine algebraic geometry foundations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Use advanced algebraic structures and correspondences.
decks.title: Graduate Algebra

outcomes.description: Prove the finite Galois correspondence and calculate automorphism groups, intermediate fields and solvability consequences for concrete polynomials.
Analyze modules over principal ideal domains, tensor products and finite-group representations; derive structure and character decompositions.
Use localization, Noetherian rings and ideal-variety correspondence; compute elementary affine examples and explain dimension and singularities with stated theorem hypotheses.

practice: Develop a complete Galois or representation calculation and an affine-variety example, supplying proofs rather than relying on symbolic software output.

includes: Homology, cohomology, global differential forms, connections, geodesics and Riemannian curvature.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Connect global topology with smooth and metric geometry.
decks.title: Global Geometry and Algebraic Topology

outcomes.description: Construct chain complexes and calculate simplicial or cellular homology and basic cohomology products; use exact sequences to distinguish spaces.
Prove manifold integration and Stokes results using charts and partitions of unity; compute de Rham classes and explain their topological correspondence.
Derive covariant derivatives, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and curvature tensors; calculate curvature and parallel transport for explicit metrics.

practice: Compute global invariants and curvature for selected manifolds and explain which conclusions depend on topology, smooth structure or metric.

includes: Conditional expectation, filtrations, martingales, continuous-time Markov processes, Brownian motion and Itô calculus.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Analyze random evolution with measure-theoretic tools.
decks.title: Stochastic Processes

outcomes.description: Define conditional expectation and martingales on filtered probability spaces; prove selected convergence and stopping results with integrability conditions.
Construct Poisson and continuous-time Markov processes and Brownian motion; derive generators, transition equations and stationary behavior.
Define Itô integrals, apply Itô's formula and solve elementary stochastic differential equations; compare strong, weak and deterministic interpretations.

practice: Prove a stopping or convergence claim and derive an SDE model's moments and stationary law, checking every probabilistic assumption.

includes: First-order syntax and semantics, completeness, incompleteness, axiomatic sets, ordinals and cardinals.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Analyze mathematical reasoning and its formal limits.
decks.title: Mathematical Logic and Foundations

outcomes.description: Construct formal derivations and models; prove soundness and a first-order completeness theorem through an explicit model-construction argument.
Encode syntax arithmetically and explain diagonalization; prove a precisely stated incompleteness result and distinguish truth, provability and decidability.
Reason within elementary set axioms about ordinals, cardinals and choice; distinguish theorem dependence and relative consistency from contradiction.

practice: Write a formal proof and countermodel pair, then develop a carefully delimited metatheorem with its encoding and consistency assumptions.

includes: Retrosynthesis, selectivity, protecting groups, organometallic reactions, catalytic cycles and route evaluation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Design and evaluate multistep molecular construction.
decks.title: Organic Synthesis and Organometallic Methods

outcomes.description: Develop retrosynthetic disconnections and forward routes using carbon-carbon bond formation, oxidation-reduction and stereoselective transformations; justify selectivity and compatibility.
Construct organometallic catalytic cycles using electron counting, oxidative addition, insertion and elimination; predict ligand and substrate effects within stated models.
Compare routes by yield, step economy, impurity control, hazards and waste; specify characterization evidence and contingency plans.

practice: Defend two competing multistep syntheses and perform an approved small-scale segment or analyze authentic execution and characterization records.

includes: Polymer synthesis and architecture, crystals and defects, processing, phase behavior and material-property measurements.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Relate chemical structure and processing to material function.
decks.title: Materials and Polymer Chemistry

outcomes.description: Compare step-growth, chain-growth and network polymerization; calculate conversion and molecular-weight distributions in explicitly taught ideal models.
Relate crystal defects, bonding, morphology and phase diagrams to thermal, mechanical, electronic and interfacial properties of polymers, ceramics and functional solids.
Select synthesis, processing and characterization strategies for a material specification; justify durability, recyclability and life-cycle tradeoffs from evidence.

practice: Design a polymer or functional-material comparison using thermal, mechanical and structural data and a documented processing-property hypothesis.

includes: Atmospheric, aquatic and soil chemistry, geochemical speciation, contaminant fate, source inference and remediation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain chemical behavior in environmental systems.
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry and Geochemistry

outcomes.description: Calculate compartment mass balances, speciation, redox, sorption, partitioning and reaction-loss predictions using explicitly taught equilibrium and finite-time fate models.
Design contamination sampling and chemical source-discrimination studies; evaluate atmospheric, water or soil evidence and compare remediation options with uncertainty and exposure consequences.

practice: Investigate a supplied watershed, air-quality or soil case, close chemical balances and defend a source and remediation conclusion against alternatives.

includes: Physical-organic mechanisms, transition states, isotope effects, electronic structure, ligand dynamics and advanced catalysis.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Discriminate molecular mechanisms through quantitative evidence.
decks.title: Advanced Molecular Reactivity

outcomes.description: Derive mechanistic predictions from transition-state models, substituent effects, isotope effects and stereoelectronics; distinguish competing organic pathways using kinetic and spectral evidence.
Analyze ligand-field and molecular-orbital descriptions, spin states, electron transfer and ligand substitution; reconcile inorganic catalytic cycles with rates, spectra and thermodynamics.

practice: Develop a mechanism-discrimination dossier with quantitative predictions, conflicting evidence and a proposed decisive experiment for an organic or inorganic catalyst.

includes: Self-consistent electronic calculations, molecular force fields, molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo and free-energy estimation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Compute molecular properties while auditing physical and numerical approximations.
decks.title: Computational Chemistry and Molecular Simulation

outcomes.description: Implement a minimal-basis restricted Hartree-Fock self-consistent loop from supplied integrals; use documented electronic-structure software to compare basis, correlation and density-functional errors.
Implement classical force evaluation and velocity-Verlet integration with periodic boundaries; analyze ensembles, constraints, biomolecular force fields and sampling adequacy.
Implement Metropolis sampling and bounded free-energy reweighting or umbrella integration; estimate correlated-sample uncertainty and validate molecular thermodynamic predictions.

practice: Implement toy electronic and molecular simulations, then audit a small-molecule or biomolecular calculation against convergence, sampling and experimental checks.

includes: Hyphenated separations, tandem mass spectrometry, multidimensional NMR, sensors, multivariate calibration and analytical validation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Develop and validate advanced chemical measurement systems.
decks.title: Advanced Analytical Methods and Chemometrics

outcomes.description: Design LC-MS/MS, two-dimensional NMR or coupled sensor measurements; derive how separation, fragmentation, coherence or transduction constrains chemical identification.

Construct multivariate calibration and spectral unmixing using covariance eigenmodels, constrained least squares and explicitly taught latent-component regression; diagnose nonuniqueness and matrix effects.
Validate a method through traceability, reference materials, recovery, robustness and interlaboratory evidence; justify uncertainty and fitness-for-purpose claims.

practice: Develop an advanced analytical workflow from raw signals to validated composition, challenging it with blinded mixtures and interferents.

includes: Analog electronics, amplification, noise, sampling, Fourier signal analysis, acquisition and experimental inference.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Build calibrated measurement chains and test physical explanations.
decks.title: Experimental Physics and Instrumentation

outcomes.description: Design amplifier and filter circuits using taught operational-amplifier models; calculate transfer functions, noise budgets, sampling limits and lock-in detection responses.
Acquire and analyze time-series or spectral signals using documented data-acquisition and FFT procedures; estimate calibration, parameter uncertainty and systematic bias.
Design an experiment that distinguishes physical models; justify instrument choice, controls, safety, uncertainty allocation and transparent handling of anomalous data.

practice: Build and calibrate a sensor-amplifier-acquisition chain and investigate a weak signal with spectral, noise and systematic-error analyses.

includes: Continuum conservation laws, stress, elasticity, viscous fluids, boundary layers and geophysical flow approximations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Model deformable solids and moving fluids.
decks.title: Continuum Mechanics and Fluids

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances and stress-strain relations in Cartesian tensor notation; solve elementary elastic deformation and wave problems.
Derive and nondimensionalize Navier-Stokes equations; analyze vorticity, pipe flow, boundary layers and rotating or stratified geophysical approximations.
Implement a bounded continuum discretization and compare with analytic or measured benchmarks; assess constitutive assumptions, boundary conditions and resolution.

practice: Analyze and simulate a two-dimensional flow or elastic-wave problem, documenting dimensionless regimes and experimental or manufactured-solution validation.

includes: Lorentz transformations, Minkowski geometry, relativistic energy-momentum and elementary four-vector dynamics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict measurements across inertial reference frames.
decks.title: Special Relativity

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations, intervals, simultaneity, proper time and Doppler shifts using spacetime diagrams and four-vectors.
Solve relativistic collisions, thresholds and constant-proper-acceleration examples using invariant energy-momentum and clearly distinguished coordinate quantities.

practice: Analyze a relativistic collision and clock experiment in two frames and prove agreement of invariant predictions.

includes: Classical and quantum ensembles, interacting systems, critical phenomena and near-equilibrium response.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Explain collective thermal behavior beyond ideal systems.
decks.title: Graduate Statistical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive grand-canonical, Bose and Fermi distributions and evaluate ideal quantum gases, correlation functions and ensemble equivalence or failure.
Analyze Ising and mean-field models, order parameters and scaling; derive one-dimensional transfer-matrix results and elementary coarse-graining recursions.
Derive master-equation balance, transport coefficients and linear-response or fluctuation-dissipation relations for explicitly specified near-equilibrium models.

practice: Compare exact, mean-field and coarse-grained predictions for an interacting model and derive a measurable equilibrium or transport response.

includes: Scattering, propagators, path integrals, identical particles, second quantization, mixed states and open quantum systems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Use graduate quantum representations and approximation machinery.
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive propagator and scattering formulations, partial-wave and Born approximations and elementary path integrals; calculate amplitudes with normalization and unitarity checks.
Construct bosonic and fermionic Fock states and second-quantized Hamiltonians; calculate elementary many-particle matrix elements and correlations.
Use density operators, partial traces, entanglement measures and quantum channels; derive bounded master-equation models and analyze decoherence and measurement protocols.

practice: Calculate a scattering observable and an open two-level-system evolution in complementary representations, checking approximation and probability preservation.

includes: Atomic structure, angular coupling, fine and hyperfine effects, lasers, coherent optics and spectroscopy.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect light-matter mechanisms with controlled measurements.
decks.title: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary multielectron, fine, hyperfine and external-field shifts using angular coupling and controlled perturbative models.
Derive two-level driven dynamics and laser rate equations; explain coherence, linewidths, resonators and bounded cooling or trapping mechanisms.
Infer transition strengths, temperatures or interaction parameters from calibrated spectra; distinguish line broadening, instrumental response and model ambiguity.

practice: Analyze or conduct an approved spectroscopy experiment and discriminate physical linewidth or level-shift mechanisms with quantitative predictions.

includes: Crystal and reciprocal lattices, diffraction, phonons, electronic bands, transport, semiconductors and collective phases.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Explain emergent properties of solids from microscopic structure.
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices and diffraction conditions; derive elementary lattice-vibration dispersions and phonon heat capacities.
Derive Bloch, nearly-free-electron and tight-binding models; calculate band occupation, effective mass and elementary metal or semiconductor transport.
Compare magnetic order and superconductivity using explicitly developed exchange and mean-field pairing models; infer phases from structural, thermal and transport evidence.

practice: Infer a material's lattice and electronic model from diffraction and transport data and test competing explanations of a phase transition.

includes: Nuclear structure and reactions, radioactive decay, elementary particles, symmetries, collision observables and detectors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Infer subatomic structure through reactions and detection.
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate binding, decay chains, reaction thresholds and simple liquid-drop or shell-model predictions; infer nuclear size and structure from scattering evidence.
Organize particles and interactions by quantum numbers and symmetries; calculate elementary collision kinematics and interpret cross sections without assuming field-theoretic amplitudes.
Explain energy loss, tracking, calorimetry and counting detectors; reconstruct bounded events and estimate efficiency, background and statistical significance.

practice: Reconstruct a supplied decay or collision dataset and compare candidate particle or nuclear models with detector and background effects included.

includes: Radiative diagnostics, stellar structure, orbital and galactic dynamics, distance inference and introductory cosmology.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Infer astronomical systems from limited remote evidence.
decks.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology

outcomes.description: Derive elementary radiative-transfer and stellar-structure equations; connect spectra, hydrostatic balance, nuclear energy budgets and stellar evolutionary stages.
Analyze planetary orbits, transit and velocity signals, stellar distances and galaxy rotation; separate observational selection from inferred mass or population structure.
Apply explicitly taught homogeneous-expansion and Friedmann models to redshift, distances and thermal history; assess evidence for dark matter and dark energy and model limits.

practice: Fit a stellar, planetary or cosmological dataset using explicit forward observables, distance assumptions and selection-bias checks.

includes: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein equations, black-hole and cosmological metrics, geodesics and linearized gravitational waves.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive gravitational dynamics in curved spacetime.
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Construct Lorentzian metrics, stress-energy tensors and curvature; derive geodesic and Einstein equations from geometric and variational principles.
Analyze Schwarzschild and homogeneous cosmological solutions, horizons, orbital tests and proper-time observables with coordinate-singularity checks.
Linearize field equations under specified gauge conditions; derive gravitational-wave propagation and leading observable detector or cosmological consequences.

practice: Derive a metric's curvature and observable geodesics and analyze a linear perturbation with invariant and limiting-case checks.

includes: Classical fields, relativistic quantization, propagators, perturbative scattering, regularization, renormalization and gauge foundations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Compute relativistic quantum observables from field models.
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

outcomes.description: Derive scalar, spinor and electromagnetic field equations and Noether currents; quantize free fields with canonical or path-integral representations.
Derive propagators and Feynman rules and calculate bounded tree-level and one-loop amplitudes with symmetry, dimensional and unitarity checks.
Regularize and renormalize a specified elementary model; derive running couplings and explain gauge constraints, effective theories and perturbative limits.

practice: Carry a simple interacting field theory from action to a renormalized observable, documenting conventions, diagrams and approximation boundaries.

includes: Particle and field simulation, eigenproblems, Monte Carlo, physical invariants and computational validation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Implement and validate computational physical models.
decks.title: Computational Physics

outcomes.description: Implement symplectic particle integration and finite-grid wave or Schrödinger evolution; compare discretization choices through conservation, stability and spectral errors.
Implement Metropolis sampling for a spin or particle model; calculate thermodynamic observables and estimate autocorrelation-aware uncertainty by blocking.
Design verification and validation studies using analytic limits, manufactured solutions, refinement, independent implementations and measured evidence.

practice: Deliver a reproducible physical simulation with implementation tests, invariant tracking, uncertainty analysis and comparison against independent evidence.

includes: Neural circuits, sensory and motor systems, plasticity, behavior, bounded computational models and experimental inference.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect neural mechanisms to information processing and behavior.
decks.title: Neuroscience and Behavior

outcomes.description: Explain synaptic integration, sensory coding, motor control, plasticity and learning through anatomically explicit circuit diagrams and comparative behavioral evidence.
Calculate an explicitly taught discrete-time integrate-and-fire model and population-rate code; distinguish model states, observables and biological limitations.
Interpret electrophysiology, imaging, lesion and stimulation studies; distinguish correlation, representation and causal necessity and justify ethical experimental choices.

practice: Analyze neural and behavioral time series, compare a bounded circuit model with alternatives and design a discriminating intervention.

includes: Biodiversity assessment, detection, population viability, conservation genetics, restoration and resource-management decisions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Translate ecological evidence into defensible conservation action.
decks.title: Conservation and Applied Ecology

outcomes.description: Estimate abundance and occupancy using explicitly taught mark-recapture and repeated-detection likelihoods; construct finite-stage viability projections and assess sampling uncertainty.
Compare habitat protection, restoration, harvest and genetic-management options using ecological predictions, costs, indigenous or community interests and uncertainty-sensitive decision criteria.

practice: Produce a conservation assessment from imperfect survey data and defend an intervention against ecological, social and uncertainty tradeoffs.

includes: Sequence processing, assembly, alignment, genomic variation, expression analysis, reproducibility and genomic governance.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer genomic structure and function computationally.
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics

outcomes.description: Implement k-mer counting, dynamic-programming alignment and a small graph assembly; run documented read-quality, mapping and annotation workflows with reference-bias checks.
Infer variants and differential expression using explicitly taught count and error models; apply multiple-testing control and compare phylogenetic or functional explanations.
Create reproducible genomic workflows with metadata and provenance; justify consent, reidentification, ancestry-reference and data-sharing decisions.

practice: Analyze an approved or public sequencing dataset from reads to a biological claim, including an implemented algorithm and independent validation.

includes: Biochemical reaction networks, stochastic simulation, parameter inference, identifiability and perturbation-based validation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Build and challenge quantitative biological mechanism models.
decks.title: Systems and Quantitative Biology

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric ODE and chemical-master-equation models; implement Gillespie event sampling with derived propensities and waiting-time distributions.
Estimate network parameters and uncertainty from time series; analyze structural or practical identifiability, sensitivity and competing causal network explanations.
Design informative perturbations and cross-condition predictions; evaluate model adequacy using held-out data, conservation laws and biological plausibility.

practice: Implement deterministic and stochastic versions of a regulatory network, fit imperfect data and design a perturbation separating rival mechanisms.

includes: Chromatin, transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation, proteostasis and advanced molecular perturbation strategies.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Evaluate molecular regulatory mechanisms at graduate experimental depth.
decks.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Regulation

outcomes.description: Compare chromatin, transcription, RNA processing and protein-turnover mechanisms using explicit occupancy, feedback and molecular-interaction models and their limitations.
Design complementary perturbation, reporter, chromatin-assay, proteomic and imaging studies; interpret supplied processed data while controlling specificity, timing and indirect effects.

practice: Critically reconstruct a regulatory mechanism from conflicting experimental records and defend a multi-assay causal test with quantitative predictions.

includes: Macromolecular structural representations, crystallographic and cryo-EM forward models, NMR restraints, reconstruction and validation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Recover and assess macromolecular structure from indirect observations.
decks.title: Structural Biology and Biophysics

outcomes.description: Construct discrete three-dimensional density, Fourier-scattering and projection models and interpret NMR distance restraints; explain phases, orientation, resolution and conformational heterogeneity.

Implement a two-dimensional regularized least-squares reconstruction and use documented crystallographic or cryo-EM refinement workflows; distinguish algorithmic priors from observed structural evidence.
Validate models using held-out measurements, map agreement, stereochemistry and alternative conformations; infer binding or functional consequences without overstating resolution.

practice: Reconstruct a toy density and audit a public macromolecular model against maps or restraints, including nonuniqueness and held-out validation.

includes: Coalescent and demographic inference, ecological-evolutionary dynamics, spatial patches and hierarchical population models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer evolutionary history and coupled population processes.
decks.title: Graduate Eco-Evolutionary Modeling

outcomes.description: Derive and simulate finite-population and coalescent ancestry models; compare demographic, selective and gene-flow explanations through explicitly constructed sequence likelihoods.
Analyze coupled ecological-evolutionary ODE and discrete-patch models using equilibria, stability, invasion criteria and numerical perturbations.
Fit hierarchical population or comparative models with explicitly taught latent-state and observation likelihoods; assess identifiability, detection bias and out-of-sample prediction.

practice: Fit and compare coupled demographic or ecological models using synthetic recovery tests and independent biological observations.

includes: Epidemiological study designs, disease measures, causal bias, discrete epidemic models and population-health decisions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Evaluate population disease evidence and interventions.
decks.title: Epidemiology and Population Health

outcomes.description: Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk ratios, odds ratios and diagnostic predictive values; compare cohort, case-control and trial designs and identify selection or confounding bias.
Construct and calculate explicit discrete-time susceptible-infectious-recovered models, reproduction thresholds and intervention scenarios; state mixing and observation assumptions.
Compare intervention evidence, uncertainty, unequal burdens and individual or collective obligations; justify a population-health decision without claiming clinical authorization.

practice: Analyze an outbreak or chronic-disease dataset, test an alternative causal explanation and defend a proportionate intervention with sensitivity analysis.

includes: Contained genetic engineering, expression design, screening, bioprocess balances and biotechnology governance.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Design and evaluate biological engineering workflows.
decks.title: Biotechnology and Synthetic Biology

outcomes.description: Design benign recombinant expression or editing constructs, assembly and screening workflows; explain specificity, controls, off-target assessment and genotype-to-function validation.
Calculate batch-growth and product balances using explicitly taught yield and saturation models; compare expression, purification and scale-up constraints.
Evaluate containment, ecological uncertainty, intellectual property, access and dual-use implications; justify a design restriction or alternative using evidence.

practice: Design and validate a benign contained biosensor or production workflow through approved experiments or execution records, including failure and governance analyses.

includes: Camera calibration, geometric reconstruction, image restoration, recognition, segmentation and vision evaluation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Infer scene structure and meaning from images.
decks.title: Computer Vision

outcomes.description: Implement camera calibration, correspondence, triangulation and bounded image-restoration objectives; analyze geometric ambiguity, noise and regularization.
Train and evaluate recognition or segmentation models; compare geometric and learned representations using localization errors, domain shifts, subgroup performance and uncertainty.

practice: Recover a small scene from calibrated images and evaluate a recognition pipeline under altered illumination, viewpoint and data distribution.

includes: Entropy, source coding, mutual information, channel capacity and elementary error-correcting codes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Quantify information and communication limits.
decks.title: Information Theory and Coding

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy, relative entropy and mutual information; derive source-coding bounds and implement prefix and arithmetic coding.
Define noisy-channel capacity and derive binary and Gaussian examples; develop typical-sequence arguments for bounded coding theorems with stated asymptotic assumptions.
Construct and decode elementary linear error-correcting codes using parity-check matrices; compare correction guarantees, rate and empirical channel performance.

practice: Implement a compression-and-transmission chain and compare finite-length performance with proven entropy and error-correction bounds.

includes: Randomized algorithms, approximation, linear-programming relaxations and advanced time or space complexity.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Design algorithms and prove advanced performance limits.
decks.title: Graduate Algorithms and Complexity

outcomes.description: Design randomized sampling, hashing and graph algorithms; derive expectation and high-probability bounds using explicitly developed concentration arguments.
Construct approximation algorithms through greedy analysis, primal-dual methods and linear-program rounding; prove approximation ratios and compare integrality gaps.
Prove selected hierarchy and space-complexity results; analyze randomized and parameterized classes and distinguish restricted lower bounds from unresolved general claims.

practice: Implement an advanced algorithm, prove its guarantee and construct adversarial examples exposing the gap between theory and average empirical behavior.

includes: Consensus, replication, consistency, failure detectors, distributed transactions and service evaluation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Build distributed services under explicit failure assumptions.
decks.title: Graduate Distributed Systems

outcomes.description: Specify safety and liveness and implement a replicated consensus log under crash and message failures; verify leader changes and state-machine execution.
Prove elementary impossibility and quorum results, including the asynchronous consensus limitation; distinguish synchrony, fairness and failure-detector assumptions.
Design sharded transactional services and compare consistency models, recovery and availability; benchmark fault-injected workloads against stated service objectives.

practice: Build a replicated key-value service with model-based history checking, partition injection and a written safety and liveness argument.

includes: Operational and denotational semantics, type soundness, fixed points, program logics and concurrent verification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Prove language and program correctness beyond testing.
decks.title: Semantics and Formal Verification

outcomes.description: Define operational and denotational models for a small language; develop ordered-domain fixed-point semantics and prove selected equivalence or adequacy properties.
Prove progress and preservation for a typed calculus using substitution and induction; analyze polymorphism, effects or subtyping through explicit rules.
Verify stateful or concurrent programs using Hoare, separation and temporal reasoning; implement finite-state model checking and explain abstraction soundness and incompleteness.

practice: Formalize a small language and prove type safety, then verify a stateful component with machine-checked or independently reviewed proof obligations.

includes: Generalization theory, optimization behavior, representation learning, latent generative models and reproducible research evaluation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Analyze learning guarantees and advanced model behavior.
decks.title: Learning Theory and Advanced Models

outcomes.description: Derive concentration, uniform-convergence and capacity-based generalization bounds; analyze consistency and optimization assumptions and identify vacuous guarantees.
Derive and implement bounded variational, autoregressive or diffusion objectives and representation-learning methods; distinguish approximate inference, optimization and sampling errors.
Design reproducible comparative studies with ablations, scaling and distribution-shift tests; justify claims about robustness, causal interpretation, privacy and societal consequences.

practice: Reproduce a bounded advanced-learning result, derive its objective and compare theoretical claims with controlled failures and statistical uncertainty.

includes: Shared-memory and message-passing parallelism, GPU execution, memory hierarchies, scalability and numerical reproducibility.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Engineer correct and efficient parallel computations.
decks.title: Parallel and High-Performance Computing

outcomes.description: Implement shared-memory, rank-based message-passing and GPU kernels using explicitly taught synchronization and communication semantics; partition numerical workloads.
Analyze cache locality, SIMD, GPU memory, bandwidth and communication costs; derive speedup and roofline predictions and compare hardware tradeoffs.
Profile and validate parallel solvers; diagnose races, reduction-order error, load imbalance and scaling limits with reproducible benchmarks.

practice: Parallelize a numerical solver across two execution models and report correctness, numerical reproducibility, resource use and measured scalability.

includes: Security games, pseudorandomness, encryption, authentication, signatures and introductory zero-knowledge protocols.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Prove security claims under explicit computational assumptions.
decks.title: Cryptographic Foundations

outcomes.description: Define adversarial games, indistinguishability, negligible advantage and reductions; prove elementary composition or hybrid arguments and identify assumption mismatches.
Construct and analyze pseudorandom-function, authenticated-encryption and public-key signature schemes; connect algebraic operations to stated hardness assumptions.
Analyze a bounded interactive identification or zero-knowledge protocol through completeness, soundness and simulation; distinguish proof-model security from implementation leakage.

practice: Write a full game-based reduction and implement a toy construction for testing only, contrasting the proof with nonce, timing and validation failures.

includes: Rigid-body kinematics, feedback control, state estimation, localization and collision-aware motion planning.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Integrate physical models, sensing and action in embodied systems.
decks.title: Robotics and Control

outcomes.description: Construct rigid-body transformations and manipulator Jacobians; derive bounded dynamics, linear feedback and finite-horizon quadratic control using stability and Riccati recursions.
Derive Kalman and extended-Kalman prediction-update equations from Gaussian state and observation models; implement localization and diagnose observability and inconsistent uncertainty.
Implement configuration-space collision checking and sampling-based motion planning; integrate planning, estimation and feedback and evaluate safety under model and sensor errors.

practice: Implement a simulated mobile robot or manipulator with noisy sensors, constrained planning and feedback; validate estimation consistency and failure-safe behavior.
